## Motivation

`/rerun-test` reruns chosen test files on a PR, each on the runner it is registered for, but only for CUDA and CPU. A file registered with `register_amd_ci` gets "rerun-test.yml has no AMD job". So an AMD-only test, or the AMD registration of a shared test, cannot be rerun from a PR comment. The CI States tip still points every PR at `/rerun-test`.

## Modifications

- `/rerun-test --amd <specs>` and `/rerun-group --amd <groups>` run the specs on the AMD runners of their `register_amd_ci` suites instead of NV. A file registered on several AMD pools fans out to one dispatch per pool, as CUDA does. Without `--amd`, nothing changes for NV.
- `rerun-test.yml` gains an `amd` mode and a `rerun-test-amd` job. It brings up the CI container the way `pr-test-amd.yml` does (`ensure_vram_clear.sh`, `amd_ci_start_container.sh`, `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`), then runs each file directly through `amd_ci_exec.sh`, like the CUDA job does. It uses `max-parallel: 2`, because AMD runners are shared with PR CI. The Docker Hub login is passed only when `pr_head_sha` is empty, so fork code never receives it. That is the same rule as `HF_MUSE_SPARK_TOKEN`.
- `partition_rerun_tests.py`: AMD estimates are used for partitioning and for the 60-minute limit. NV estimates are byte-identical to before.
- For now, the suite-to-runner table is `AMD_SUITE_RUNNERS`, kept in sync with the AMD workflows by `scripts/lint/check_amd_rerun_runners.py`. Once #47946 lands, it reads `amd_runner_configs` the way the CUDA path reads `runner_configs`, and the dict and the lint go away.
- The skill and the contribution guide document `--amd`.

## Verification

Offline, with a mocked GitHub API:

- All 3115 test specs resolve identically for NV. The only differences are the error texts for AMD-only files, which now suggest `--amd`.
- The NV `estimate_seconds` values (all files across 11 runners plus cpu) and the NV partitions are byte-identical.
- `--amd` resolves 372 (file, runner) entries and rejects nightly and disaggregation suites with a reason.

An end-to-end test of the command on this PR follows below.

 ## Post
 
-Put every spec in one comment, for example `/rerun-test registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage_file_backend.py registered/lora/test_lora_update.py`. The handler replies with the run links and marks the reply when the runs finish.
+Put every spec in one comment, for example `/rerun-test registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage_file_backend.py registered/lora/test_lora_update.py`. The handler replies with the run links and marks the reply when the runs finish. Add `--amd` (to `/rerun-test` or `/rerun-group`) to run the specs on the AMD runners of their `register_amd_ci` suites instead (per-commit and extra suites only); AMD runners are scarce, so use it for ROCm-relevant changes.
 
 ## Limits
 
 - A file estimated above 60 minutes is rejected; it runs only in its scheduled tier.
 - CPU tests run only for the ubuntu CPU suite (`base-a-test-cpu`); Xeon and arm64 suites are not supported.

+- On NV, no PR-local `sglang-kernel` wheel is built. A change under `python/sglang/kernels/aot/` needs the normal PR CI there; `--amd` reruns do build it.
 - Each file runs directly (`python3 <file> -f`), not through `test/run_suite.py`, and `/run-cpu-ci` runs main's stage workflow. A change to the CI runner itself (`run_suite.py`, `ci_utils.py`, `fork_test_worker.py`, the stage workflows) is validated by the PR's own PR Test run.
 
 Command syntax and permissions: [contribution guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests).

+        description: "Dispatch mode: cuda | multimodal_gen | cpu | amd"

@@ -455,8 +456,112 @@ jobs:
           fi
           echo "All $total test(s) passed in ${total_elapsed}s"
 
+  # Same container bring-up as pr-test-amd.yml, but runs each file directly.
+  rerun-test-amd:
+    name: rerun-test-amd (partition ${{ matrix.partition }})
+    needs: prepare-partitions
+    if: inputs.mode == 'amd'
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      # AMD runners are shared with PR CI and far fewer than NV ones.
+      max-parallel: 2
+      matrix: ${{ fromJson(needs.prepare-partitions.outputs.matrix) }}
+    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runs_on }}
+    # Image pull, AOT kernel build and install run before the 60-min test step.
+    timeout-minutes: 150
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      issues: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout code
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ inputs.pr_head_sha || github.sha }}
+          # This checkout can hold a fork's code that the steps below execute;
+          # without this the job token stays in .git/config, readable by it.
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Mark runner picked up
+        if: inputs.reply_comment_id != '' && inputs.reply_marker != ''
+        continue-on-error: true
+        env:
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          python3 scripts/ci/utils/update_rerun_test_status.py \
+            --comment-id "${{ inputs.reply_comment_id }}" \
+            --marker "${{ inputs.reply_marker }}" \
+            --status running \
+            --repo "${{ github.repository }}"
+
+      - uses: ./.github/actions/check-maintenance
+
+      - name: Ensure VRAM is clear
+        run: bash scripts/ci/amd/ensure_vram_clear.sh rocm
+
+      - name: Start CI container
+        env:
+          GITHUB_WORKSPACE: ${{ github.workspace }}
+          # Fork code (pr_head_sha set) runs these scripts, so it gets no
+          # Docker Hub login and pulls anonymously, as its PR runs do.
+          DOCKERHUB_AMD_USERNAME: ${{ inputs.pr_head_sha == '' && secrets.DOCKERHUB_AMD_USERNAME || '' }}
+          DOCKERHUB_AMD_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.pr_head_sha == '' && secrets.DOCKERHUB_AMD_TOKEN || '' }}
+        run: bash scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh
+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: bash scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh
+
+      - name: Run test
+        timeout-minutes: 60
+        env:
+          TEST_COMMAND: ${{ matrix.test_command }}
+          RUNS_ON: ${{ inputs.runs_on }}
+        run: |
+          # The container does not inherit the job env; pass what the tests read.
+          amd_extra_envs=(-e "SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=$SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS")
+          # Same env as the 4-GPU jobs in pr-test-amd.yml and pr-test-amd-extra.yml.
+          if [[ "$RUNS_ON" == *-4gpu-* ]]; then
+            amd_extra_envs+=(-e NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 -e NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0 -e RCCL_MSCCL_ENABLE=0 -e SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1)
+          fi
+          cmds=()
+          while IFS= read -r cmd; do
+            [ -z "$cmd" ] && continue
+            cmds+=("$cmd")
+          done <<< "$TEST_COMMAND"
+          total=${#cmds[@]}
+          failed=()
+          suite_start=$SECONDS
+          for idx in "${!cmds[@]}"; do
+            i=$((idx + 1))
+            cmd="${cmds[$idx]}"
+            echo ""
+            echo "."
+            echo "Begin ($i/$total): python3 $cmd"
+            echo "."
+            file_start=$SECONDS
+            if ! bash scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_exec.sh "${amd_extra_envs[@]}" \
+                -w /sglang-checkout/test python3 $cmd -f; then
+              failed+=("$cmd")
+            fi
+            elapsed=$(( SECONDS - file_start ))
+            echo "."
+            echo "End ($i/$total): elapsed=${elapsed}s"
+            echo "."
+            echo ""
+          done
+          total_elapsed=$(( SECONDS - suite_start ))
+          if [ ${#failed[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
+            echo "${#failed[@]}/$total test(s) failed in ${total_elapsed}s:"
+            printf '  %s\n' "${failed[@]}"
+            {
+              echo "### Failed tests (partition ${{ matrix.partition }})"
+              printf -- '- `%s`\n' "${failed[@]}"
+            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "All $total test(s) passed in ${total_elapsed}s"
+

+    needs: [prepare-partitions, rerun-test-cuda, rerun-test-multimodal-gen, rerun-test-cpu, rerun-test-amd]

@@ -152,7 +152,7 @@ For CI to run on a pull request, it must have the "run-ci" label. Authorized use
 - `/run-<tier>-ci`: Selects one registered tier, such as `/run-nv-extra-ci`. Applies "run-ci" and the tier's optional label, then reruns just the listed workflows, including ones that already succeeded.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Check AMD_SUITE_RUNNERS in scripts/ci/partition_rerun_tests.py against the AMD PR-test workflows.
+
+`/rerun-test --amd` sends a file to the runner its suite maps to there. Every
+suite those workflows run through run_suite.py must map to the runner of the
+job that runs it, so a rerun reproduces that job.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+import re
+import sys
+
+import yaml
+
+PARTITION_SCRIPT = "scripts/ci/partition_rerun_tests.py"
+WORKFLOWS = (
+    ".github/workflows/pr-test-amd.yml",
+    ".github/workflows/pr-test-amd-extra.yml",
+)
+# Run by the workflows above but deliberately not dispatchable by /rerun-test.
+NOT_RERUNNABLE = {
+    # Needs amd_ci_start_container_disagg.sh and the RDMA setup of its own job.
+    "stage-b-test-large-8-gpu-mi35x-disaggregation-amd",
+}
+# `--suite` of test/run_suite.py; the multimodal run_suite.py takes no --hw.
+_SUITE_ARG = re.compile(r"run_suite\.py --hw amd --suite ([\w.-]+)")
+# runs-on: ${{ format('linux-{0}-1gpu-sglang', inputs.runner_arch || 'mi300') }}
+_ARCH_FORMAT = re.compile(
+    r"format\('linux-\{0\}-([\w.-]+)', inputs\.runner_arch \|\| '(\w+)'\)"
+)
+
+
+def _runner_labels(job: dict) -> set[str]:
+    runs_on = str(job.get("runs-on", ""))
+    m = _ARCH_FORMAT.search(runs_on)
+    if m:
+        return {f"linux-{m.group(2)}-{m.group(1)}"}
+    if "matrix.runner" in runs_on:
+        return set(job["strategy"]["matrix"]["runner"])
+    return {runs_on}
+
+
+def workflow_suites() -> dict[str, set[str]]:
+    """Suite -> runner labels of the jobs that run it."""
+    suites: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
+    for path in WORKFLOWS:
+        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
+            workflow = yaml.safe_load(f)
+        for job in workflow["jobs"].values():
+            for step in job.get("steps") or []:
+                run = " ".join(str(step.get("run", "")).replace("\\\n", " ").split())
+                for suite in _SUITE_ARG.findall(run):
+                    suites.setdefault(suite, set()).update(_runner_labels(job))
+    return suites
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("partition", PARTITION_SCRIPT)
+    partition = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(partition)
+    runners = partition.AMD_SUITE_RUNNERS
+    in_ci = workflow_suites()
+
+    errors = []
+    for suite, labels in sorted(in_ci.items()):
+        if suite in NOT_RERUNNABLE:
+            continue
+        if suite not in runners:
+            errors.append(
+                f"{suite}: run by the AMD PR-test workflows but missing from "
+                f"AMD_SUITE_RUNNERS (or add it to NOT_RERUNNABLE here with a reason)"
+            )
+        elif runners[suite] not in labels:
+            errors.append(
+                f"{suite}: AMD_SUITE_RUNNERS says `{runners[suite]}` but its job "
+                f"runs on {sorted(labels)}"
+            )
+    for suite in sorted(set(runners) - set(in_ci)):
+        errors.append(f"{suite}: in AMD_SUITE_RUNNERS but no AMD PR-test job runs it")
+
+    if errors:
+        print(f"ERROR: AMD_SUITE_RUNNERS in {PARTITION_SCRIPT} is out of sync:")
+        for error in errors:
+            print(f"  {error}")
+        return 1
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
